added: A new entry with no predecessor. Consumers add it.
retired: An entry removed with no successor. Its code is kept and never reused. Records classified under an earlier version stay valid under that version.
split: One entry replaced by several. Each successor carries derived_from; the retired predecessor carries superseded_by. Successors may sit in a different dimension from the predecessor. A trend series on the predecessor continues as the sum of its successors.
merged: Several entries replaced by one. The survivor carries derived_from listing each predecessor.
renamed: Same concept, different name. The code does not change, so stored records need no migration.
moved: Same concept, different dimension (for example a label/tag becoming a modus). The code does not change: codes are global, not per dimension. The entry carries moved_from.
regrouped: A modus moved to a different high-level classification. The code does not change; group_code does, and the entry carries regrouped_from.
redefined: The EBA declares that the definition was updated. The annex usually calls this a clarification, but it does not say whether the meaning changed, so treat stored records as needing review.
recited: The EBA declares that the definition was replaced with one from a different source. The EBA presents this as a change of source, not of meaning.
reworded: Observed only: the definition text differs between versions and the annex does not declare it. This repository cannot tell a cosmetic rewording from a change of meaning, and does not guess.
source_updated: Observed only: the definition text is unchanged but its cited source or link changed.
structure_changed: A change to the taxonomy's structure rather than to an entry: a dimension added, a chapter added or reordered, or a new attribute on every entry.
